hubDescription: Tree service in Nashville, TN and Davidson County: tree removal, trimming, stump grinding, storm cleanup and land clearing. Licensed, insured, free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
hubIntro: Nashville is where Triple Oak Services is based, and it is the city we know best. Davidson County has some of the most varied tree work in Middle Tennessee: century-old oaks and maples in East Nashville, Inglewood and Sylvan Park, tall hardwoods along the hills of Green Hills and Belmont, and newer infill houses squeezed beside trees that were there long before the construction started.

We handle tree removal, tree trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing across Nashville. This page covers what tree work in the city typically involves, why close-quarters jobs need more planning, and what to check before you hire a crew to remove a tree. Every job starts with a free, no-obligation estimate.

sections.h2: Older neighborhoods: East Nashville, Inglewood, Sylvan Park and Germantown
paragraphs: Nashville's older neighborhoods were laid out when streets were narrow and lots were small, and the trees planted along them have had a century to grow. In East Nashville and Inglewood, large oaks, maples and hackberries tower over bungalows and Victorians, and their crowns often reach across property lines. Sylvan Park and The Nations have a similar mix. Germantown, close to downtown and the Cumberland River, packs mature trees into very tight spaces next to brick row houses and new infill construction.

That combination makes close-quarters work the norm. A tree may sit a few feet from a roof, a neighbor's fence and an overhead service line all at once, with no room to drop it whole. We take trees down in controlled sections, lower heavy pieces under control and protect what is underneath. Crown cleaning and selective trimming are just as common, since removing dead wood and thinning a crown can keep a healthy old tree safe for years without taking it down.

sections.h2: Green Hills, Belmont, 12 South and the hillside lots
paragraphs: West and south of downtown, the terrain changes. In Green Hills, Hillsboro Village, Belmont and 12 South, lots are sloped, driveways are steep and tall hardwoods lean over homes and streets on hillsides. Access matters as much as the tree itself. A removal on a slope or behind a locked gate takes more planning than one in an open yard, and heavy equipment has to be placed carefully to avoid damaging lawns, retaining walls and pavement.

Property owners here often want a tree preserved if at all possible, and we are happy to look at pruning, cabling and crown reduction before recommending removal. When a tree does have to come down, because it is dead, diseased or leaning toward a structure, we explain the plan, give you a price and leave the site clean.

sections.h2: Storms, the Cumberland River and what they do to trees
paragraphs: Nashville's trees deal with spring thunderstorms, straight-line winds, summer drought and the occasional ice storm. The March 2020 tornado, which cut across East Nashville, Germantown and Donelson, is a reminder of how much canopy a single storm can take out and how many damaged trees remain standing afterward, with torn crowns and cracked limbs that can fail later. If a tree on your property was damaged in a storm, even if it did not fall, it is worth having it inspected.

Near the Cumberland River and its creeks, in areas like Donelson, Two Rivers, Bordeaux and Whites Creek, wet soil and flooding can weaken root systems over time. Trees leaning toward the water, trees with exposed roots and trees with sudden crown dieback are the ones we are most often asked to look at. Watch for a worsening lean, fungus at the base, large dead branches and soil lifting around the trunk.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Nashville
paragraphs: Tree rules in Metro Nashville depend on the property. Trees on public property, such as street trees and park trees, are protected, and a homeowner or contractor cannot simply remove them. Requirements for tree removal on commercial and multifamily property are different from those for a single-family yard, and development sites can carry their own conditions. Because the rules have changed over the years and can change again, check with Metro Codes or the Metro Urban Forester before removing a large tree, and check with your HOA if you have one.

Look up before any work begins. Trees touching or close to power lines, including those served by Nashville Electric Service, should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew. If anyone is in danger, call 911 first. For stump grinding or digging near the tree, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities can be marked. When we quote a job we point out lines, fences, septic fields and structures so there are no surprises on the day.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company based in Nashville. A typical job starts with a free estimate, a clear explanation of how the tree will come down and what the price includes, safe removal and a full cleanup with the debris hauled away. Stump grinding can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will solve your problem, we will tell you so.

hubFaq.a: Yes. Close-quarters removals are common in Nashville's older neighborhoods. We take trees down in controlled sections and protect roofs, fences and landscaping, and we explain the plan before work starts.

hubFaq.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Nashville?
hubFaq.a: It depends on the property. Public trees are protected, and commercial, multifamily and development sites have different requirements from single-family yards. Check with Metro Codes or the Metro Urban Forester before removing a large tree.

hubFaq.q: Do you handle storm damage and emergency removal in Nashville?
hubFaq.a: Yes, including same-day emergency removal where scheduling allows. If a power line is involved or anyone is in danger, call 911 and your utility first, then call us.

tree-trimming-pruning.title: Tree Trimming & Pruning in Nashville, TN | Triple Oak Services
tree-trimming-pruning.description: Tree trimming and pruning in Nashville, TN: dead limb removal, crown thinning, clearance from roofs and lines, storm-risk reduction. Licensed, insured, free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Nashville's mature canopy is one of its best features, but old trees need maintenance. In East Nashville, Sylvan Park, Green Hills and Belmont, big oaks, maples and hickories build up dead wood, spread over roofs and chimneys and catch wind like a sail. Crown cleaning and thinning remove the dead and crossing branches, reduce the weight on long limbs and let wind pass through, which lowers the chance of a limb failing in a thunderstorm.

Clearance work is common too: pulling limbs off roofs, siding and gutters, opening up space over driveways, and keeping branches away from service lines. Property owners in older neighborhoods usually want trees preserved, so we focus on pruning that follows the tree's natural shape rather than cutting everything back.
We do not top trees. Topping weakens them, invites decay and leaves branches that are more likely to break later. We explain what will be removed and why before any cutting begins.

faq.q: How often should I have my trees trimmed in Nashville?
faq.a: Many mature trees benefit from a check every few years, and fast-growing or storm-prone trees may need it more often. Dead wood and limbs over structures should be dealt with as soon as you see them.

faq.q: Can trimming save a tree you would otherwise remove?
faq.a: Often, yes. Removing dead wood, thinning heavy crowns and reducing weight on long limbs can keep a healthy tree safe. We will tell you honestly when trimming is enough.

stump-grinding.title: Stump Grinding in Nashville, TN | Triple Oak Services
stump-grinding.description: Stump grinding in Nashville, TN: stumps ground below grade, root flare removal and cleanup so your yard is ready to use. Free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: A stump is a problem you can trip over, mow around and watch rot for years. Grinding it below grade lets you fill the hole, lay sod, plant or build over the spot. In Nashville, the work ranges from small stumps in tight yards in Inglewood and Germantown, where the machine has to fit through a gate, to big hardwood stumps on larger lots in Green Hills, Donelson and Bordeaux.

Older Nashville neighborhoods often have buried lines, old foundations and large root systems around a stump, so the job needs a look first. Call Tennessee 811 before any digging or grinding so buried utilities are marked, and we will go over access, depth and cleanup with you during the estimate.
Stump grinding pairs well with removal. If a tree is coming down anyway, ask us to grind the stump on the same visit.

faq.q: Can your equipment fit in a narrow Nashville backyard?
faq.a: Often, yes. Access is one of the first things we check during the estimate, since gates, fences and slopes determine what equipment can reach the stump.
Below grade, deep enough to fill and plant over. Tell us what you plan to put there and we will size the job to match.

storm-damage-cleanup.title: Storm Damage Tree Cleanup in Nashville, TN | Emergency Removal | Triple Oak Services
storm-damage-cleanup.description: Storm damage tree cleanup in Nashville, TN: fallen trees, hanging limbs and emergency removal, including same-day service when available. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Nashville knows what a single storm can do to its trees. The March 2020 tornado took out huge amounts of canopy in East Nashville, Germantown and Donelson, and ordinary spring thunderstorms still bring down limbs and whole trees onto roofs, cars and fences across Davidson County. Torn crowns and cracked limbs left behind after a storm can also fail days or weeks later.

If a tree has fallen or a large limb is hanging, make sure everyone is safe first. If a power line is involved or anyone is in danger, call 911 and Nashville Electric Service before anything else, then call us. We handle storm damage and emergency tree removal, including same-day emergency removal where scheduling allows, and we cut and clear trees from roofs, yards and driveways.

After the emergency is handled, we are glad to look at the trees that stayed standing. Cracked trunks, loosened soil around the base and hanging branches are the ones worth dealing with before the next storm.

faq.q: Do you offer same-day emergency tree removal in Nashville?
faq.a: Yes, where scheduling allows. Call 615-561-0472, tell us what has fallen and where, and we will tell you how quickly we can get there.

faq.q: A tree fell on my house. What should I do first?
faq.a: Get everyone out and away from the damage. If a power line is involved or anyone is hurt, call 911 and the utility. Photograph the damage for your insurer, then call us for removal.

land-clearing-maintenance.title: Land Clearing in Nashville, TN | Brush & Lot Clearing | Triple Oak Services
land-clearing-maintenance.description: Land clearing in Nashville, TN and Davidson County: brush, undergrowth, lot and driveway clearing and property line cleanup. Free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Inside the city, land clearing usually means reclaiming an overgrown lot: thick brush and vines on a vacant parcel in Bordeaux or Whites Creek, back lots and fence lines in Donelson and Antioch, or an infill lot that needs to be opened up before a build. Left alone for a few seasons, honeysuckle, privet and volunteer trees can take over, hide property lines and become a fire and pest problem.

A typical job removes brush and undergrowth, takes out the trees that are in the way, grinds stumps if needed and leaves a clean, usable site. We walk the property first so we know what stays, what goes and where equipment can get in, then give you a clear price before work begins.
If clearing is part of a development or build, check with Metro Nashville about permits, tree-protection requirements and any approvals the project needs. We can clear to the lines you mark.

faq.q: Do you clear overgrown lots in Nashville?
faq.a: Yes. We remove brush, undergrowth, small trees and stumps so a lot is usable again. We confirm access, boundaries and price during the free estimate.

faq.q: Do I need approval before clearing land in Nashville?
faq.a: Possibly, especially for development projects. Check with Metro Nashville before clearing for a build, since tree protection and permit requirements can apply.
